text:
maria: Heads-up: we need to shift the planned kernel patch / capacity rebalance for eu-west-1 from Sat 03:00 UTC to Sat 05:30 UTC. Minimal customer impact expected, but want ops + oncall aware. Drafting status page + customer note below. Please review asap so we can send a customer notice by EOD.

jamal: ack. is this purely kernel patch (reboot) or thermal maintenance? any node drains needed?

maria: it's a kernel patch that requires node reboots for a subset of serving nodes (~12% of capacity in eu-west-1). We'll do a rolling drain with 10m stagger; autoscale will handle load. No planned model restarts. We're expecting a 90-120s reconnect per host during the drain window. No data migration.

alex: re: paging — i'll be primary oncall during the window and can take pagers. jamal, can you be secondary? also recommend we set a short SLO buffer on the router policy to fall back to eu-central1 for affected RPCs if latency spikes.

jamal: yep I can be secondary. i'll prep a quick runbook snippet and add to the oncall deck.

ops-bot: Incident bot: Scheduled maintenance event created: ID MNT-2023-1524. Notifying subscribed customers and scheduling statuspage draft. (automated)

maria: status page draft (customer-facing). This will be what we post to status.redwood.ai under "Scheduled Maintenance":

```
Status: Scheduled Maintenance
Component: eu-west-1 Inference Serving
Start: Sat, 05:30 UTC
End: Sat, 07:30 UTC (estimated)
Impact: Brief disruptions for some requests routed to eu-west-1 as hosts are rebooted. Most customers: no sustained degradation. Affected customers with pinned regions may observe transient reconnects (~2m) per host.
What we're doing: Rolling kernel patch and capacity rebalance across a subset of serving nodes. Autoscaling and routing will minimize impact; fallbacks to other regions are enabled.
Customer action: No action required. If you have strict region/pinned constraints, please reply to this thread or contact support to request a maintenance exclusion window.
```

maria: internal customer-notify template (support/customer-success):

```
Hi <CustomerName>,

We have scheduled a brief maintenance in eu-west-1 on Sat at 05:30 UTC to apply a kernel patch and rebalance capacity. We do not expect sustained downtime, but you may see short reconnects (~1-3 minutes) for traffic routed to eu-west-1.

If you have a strict requirement to avoid maintenance during that window, please reply and we'll work with you on an exclusion window.

Thanks,
Redwood Ops
```

tim: can we add a line in the customer note about contact method? like Slack + support@redwood? customers sometimes need a direct PD contact.

maria: yes good call — add: "For urgent issues during the window contact your Redwood rep or open a priority support ticket (support@redwood.ai) — include your account id." i'll update the draft.

sara: product ask: can we add a short blurb about how this reduces risk of preemption/IO stalls long-term? customers like the benefit context.

maria: added: "This patch improves scheduling stability and reduces the likelihood of transient IO stalls under heavy load." keeps it simple.

alex: runbook snippet i'm adding to the oncall doc:

```
- Pre-check (30m before): ensure canary pool active, verify autoscaler healthy, confirm fallback region routing rules set to eu-central1.
- Step 0: Post statuspage "Maintenance starting in 30m" and notify customer-success channel.
- Step 1: Begin rolling drain of subset (1 host every 10m). Monitor qps/latency on router and model endpoints.
- Step 2: If p50 latency > 300ms or error rate > 1% for 3 consecutive minutes, abort further drains and trigger emergency rollback plan (scale up standby pool in eu-central1 + notify customers).
- Step 3: After reboot and healthcheck, remove host from maintenance set.
- Post-check: Confirm all hosts back, send completion update and clear status page entry.
```

jamal: Suggest adding short pager escalation names: Primary alex, Secondary jamal, Tertiary on-call lead (maria). If alex gets paged and not responding in 5m, escalate to jamal.

maria: agreed. i'll update the schedule in ops calendar and set the oncall rota accordingly. Also tagging support to prep canned replies.

ops-bot: Reminder: Maintenance starts in 30 minutes. Auto-notifications sent to customers in affected region. (automated)

tim: support team here — prepping canned reply. i'll paste below once final. also we'll watch the customer queue and surface any customers with pinned-region flags.

maria: final checklist for publish (any objections):
- status page copy approved? (alex/jamal)
- customer-note approved? (tim/sara)
- runbook + pager rota set? (alex/jamal)
- ops calendar + tickets created? (maria)

alex: approved from SRE side. :thumbsup:

jamal: approved. adding runbook to oncall deck now.

tim: customer note approved; will broadcast and monitor replies.

sara: approved from product.

maria: ok publishing status page entry and scheduling the customer email now. i'll post a short "maintenance started" update when we begin and a completion note once done. thanks all — ping here if anything changes.
